name: Dinosaurs
hook: "Terrible lizards": the names, the eras and the extinction Jeopardy asks about again and again.

facts.label: Richard Owen
facts.statement: Sir Richard Owen coined the word "dinosaur" around 1841, from Greek words meaning "terrible lizard."

facts.label: Tyrannosaurus rex
facts.statement: Barnum Brown found the first T. rex specimen in Montana in 1902; "Scotty," unearthed in Saskatchewan, is a 42-foot, 20,000-pound example.

facts.label: Triceratops
facts.statement: Triceratops had two brow horns and one nose horn, and lived in the late Cretaceous; its name means "three-horned face."

facts.label: Stegosaurus
facts.statement: Stegosaurus means "roof lizard" in Greek, and the plated dinosaur roamed what is now Dinosaur National Monument.

facts.label: the Mesozoic era
facts.statement: The Mesozoic era, when dinosaurs roamed the Earth, is divided into the Triassic, Jurassic and Cretaceous periods.

facts.label: the extinction 65 million years ago
facts.statement: Dinosaurs died out 65 million years ago at the end of the Cretaceous; birds are their surviving descendants.

facts.label: Jurassic Park
facts.statement: Michael Crichton's novel Jurassic Park concerns the cloning of dinosaur DNA; the 1993 film starred Ariana Richards and Joseph Mazzello.
